summary: Backend-only testing of Shiprocket integration on http://localhost:8001 (preview URL is unavailable per agent note). Executed 8 pytest tests covering health, pickup locations, courier serviceability, tracking, and create-order-with-AWB endpoints. All 8 tests passed. Shiprocket authentication and API calls work end-to-end; order creation returns success=True but shipment_id/AWB are null (expected due to unconfigured warehouse per agent note).

minor.issue: Shiprocket returns null shiprocket_order_id AND null shipment_id because no warehouse is configured on the Shiprocket account. Endpoint responds success=True with message 'Order created but shipment ID not generated'. This is an account/config issue, not a code bug, but end-users will not get AWB. Consider adding a clearer error/warning when shipment_id is null.

Shiprocket rejects order_date older than 6 months. Frontend should always send current date (currently only checked implicitly). Also strict phone-number validation upstream — invalid phone (e.g. all 9s) is rejected with 422 by Shiprocket; wrap this into a clean 400 response for the client.
Endpoint uses query params pickup_pincode/delivery_pincode while Shiprocket upstream uses pickup_postcode/delivery_postcode. Inconsistent naming may confuse frontend devs — document or rename.

action_items: Configure a pickup/warehouse location in Shiprocket dashboard so shipment_id and AWB can be generated. Without this, the entire AWB flow is a no-op in production.

In /api/shiprocket/order/create-with-awb, forward upstream 4xx validation errors (invalid phone, stale order_date) as structured 400 responses instead of returning success=False + generic message so the frontend can show actionable errors.
Consider marking response as success=False when shiprocket_order_id is null; currently returns success=True even when nothing shippable was created.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 885 lines — should be split into routers (health, tracking, orders, couriers) and a shiprocket client module.
Hardcoded pickup_pincode='400001' in create_order_with_awb (line 732). Should come from actual pickup location settings or request payload.
Duplicate order-creation branches (lines 722-728, 749-756, 780-789, 804-815) can be consolidated with a helper — DRY violation.
get_shiprocket_token has no in-memory cache visible in the reviewed slice; if not cached, every request triggers a fresh login (Shiprocket tokens are valid for 10 days).
Bare `except Exception as e` swallows details in multiple places; add structured logging.
No pydantic validation on customer_phone / customer_pincode / customer_email in CreateOrderWithAWBRequest — leads to opaque 422 from Shiprocket instead of clean 400 to caller.
seed_data_creation: None. Tests create ephemeral TEST_ORDER_<ts> orders via Shiprocket; not persisted locally.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Preview URL was unavailable during this run; used http://localhost:8001. Pytest installed via pip --break-system-packages because system Python is used (per agent note about corrupted venv). Test file at /app/backend/tests/test_shiprocket.py can be reused. Shiprocket account has NO warehouse configured — expect null AWB/shipment_id in create-order response until fixed on the Shiprocket dashboard. Frontend was not tested in this iteration.
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional bugs found in code. AWB=null is an external Shiprocket account configuration issue (no warehouse) confirmed by main agent.
